{{For|Ky Fan inequality related to geometric mean arithmetic mean|Ky Fan inequality}}

In [[game theory]], the '''Ky Fan inequality''' or '''Ky Fan minimax inequality'''<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Yu |first=J. |last2=Yuan |first2=G. X. -Z. |date=1998-05-01 |title=The study of Pareto equilibria for multiobjective games by fixed point and Ky Fan minimax inequality methods |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0898122198000534 |journal=Computers & Mathematics with Applications |volume=35 |issue=9 |pages=17–24 |doi=10.1016/S0898-1221(98)00053-4 |issn=0898-1221|url-access=subscription }}</ref> is a result used to establish the existence of equilibria in various games, particularly in economics and mathematical analysis. It was introduced in Ky Fan's 1972 paper, "A minimax inequality and its applications",<ref>Fan, K. (1972) A Minimax Inequality and Applications. In: Sisha, Ed., Inequalities, Vol. 3, Academic, New York, 103-113.</ref> and is closely related to the [[Brouwer fixed-point theorem]], though often more convenient for proving equilibrium results.

The inequality applies to functions defined on compact, convex subsets of vector spaces and provides a condition under which a minimax-type inequality holds. It is frequently used in the analysis of [[non-cooperative games]], [[variational inequalities]], and [[general equilibrium]] models.

== Statement ==
Let <math>E</math> be a convex compact subset of a Hilbert space, and let <math>f : E \times E \rightarrow \mathbb{R}</math> be a function satisfying:
For every <math>y \in E</math>, the function <math>x \mapsto f(x, y)</math> is [[lower semicontinuous]].

For every <math>x \in E</math>, the function <math>y \mapsto f(x, y)</math> is [[concave function|concave]].

Then there exists <math>e \in E</math> such that:

<math>\sup_{y \in E} f(e, y) \leq \sup_{y \in E} f(y, y).</math>

This result generalizes the classic [[minimax theorem]] and is a key tool in fixed-point and equilibrium analysis.
